When multiple skills apply, process skills come first — they set the approach, then implementation skills (frontend-design, etc.) carry it out. Brainstorming and systematic-debugging are Superpowers' most common process skills, but the rule holds for any of them.

content.text:
`slugify` in `src/slug.js` now strips leading and trailing dashes, so `"  Hello World! "` becomes `"hello-world"`. I ran that example directly and got `"hello-world"`, and the three existing tests pass. I didn't add a test for the new behavior. The change is committed as `12a1d04`.

The change adds `.replace(/^-+|-+$/g, '')` after the existing replace, and I updated the comment above the function to match.

`npm test` printed a sandbox denial for `registry.npmjs.org:443`, but the tests still ran. The shell also printed `.bashrc: Permission denied` on every command, which didn't affect anything.
